jurisdiction.name: Malaysia
jurisdiction.overview: Nationally published records appear separately from applicable EU-level records. The landscape, historical relationships and legal applicability remain under document-level review.

narrative.summary: Malaysia has no AI-specific law yet: a proposed AI Governance Bill went to public consultation in July 2026 and has not been tabled. Laws touching AI include the 2024 amendments to the Personal Data Protection Act (biometric data, breach notification, data protection officers) and the Online Safety Act 2025, whose 2026 Risk Mitigation Code requires platforms to label AI-generated or manipulated content and test recommendation algorithms. National policy moved from the 2021-2025 AI Roadmap to the AI Nation 2030 action plan (2026-2030), alongside MOSTI's 2024 national AI governance and ethics guidelines and the 2025 public-sector AI adoption guidelines, with the National AI Office coordinating. Regulators add AI-relevant rules: the data protection commissioner's 2026 guideline on automated decisions and profiling and its AI framework consultation, Bank Negara's discussion paper on AI in finance, the Securities Commission's technology risk guidelines with AI principles, NACSA's AI cyber security framework and the Medical Council's AI ethics guideline. Penang and Sarawak include AI actions in their digital economy plans.
lead_institutions: Ministry of Science, Technology and Innovation
narrative.review_notes: This review was completed on 11 October 2026 and covers federal law, the federal government and ministries, regulators, and the states of Selangor, Penang and Sarawak. ASEAN instruments are shown through the regional files. Malaysia's proposed AI Governance Bill has only been put out for consultation, and its consultation paper sits behind a login, so it could only be located. Several voluntary AI codes and Selangor's AI white paper are listed as leads because they are not yet publicly available.

instruments.official_title: Garis Panduan Pengadaptasian Kecerdasan Buatan (AI) Sektor Awam
instruments.english_title: Public Sector Artificial Intelligence (AI) Adoption Guidelines
instruments.issuing_authority: National Digital Department (Jabatan Digital Negara), Ministry of Digital
instruments.current_status: Launched by the Minister of Digital on 27 February 2025 (JDN media release). JDN's policy repository lists it as guideline document No. 1 of 2025, effective 27-02-2025, status 'Masih Berkuat Kuasa' (still in force); the circulated PDF (EDARAN v2) is dated 4 March 2025. Published in Malay only; the JDN English page summarises it.
instruments.scope: Federal ministries and agencies, state governments, statutory bodies and local authorities (public sector)
instruments.summary: 158-page JDN guideline, developed with MDEC, that tells public-sector agencies how to adopt AI responsibly, complementing MOSTI's national AIGE guidelines and to be read with existing ICT rules (KRISA, PPrISA, cloud security guidelines). It sets seven AI ethics principles (data privacy and security, transparency, accountability, fairness, inclusiveness, reliability and robustness, sustainability), assigns roles to AI actors (developers, implementers, policy makers, infrastructure providers, consultants, users), lists eight adoption requirements and a step-by-step project process. It classifies public-sector AI uses into prohibited, high, limited and minimal risk tiers and provides use cases and an ethics self-assessment template for agencies.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Main whole-of-government rulebook for AI use by Malaysian public agencies, including a risk-tier classification.
instruments.evidence_reference: curl (browser user agent, --max-time 60): JDN English page read (it embeds the PDF flipbook and links the Malay page); full 158-page PDF downloaded and read (pdftotext). Launch date 27 Feb 2025 from the JDN media release (jdn.gov.my/wp-content/uploads/2025/03/SIARAN-MEDIA-MAJLIS-PELUNCURAN-GPAISA.pdf); in-force status and effective date from the JDN policy repository (dasar.jdn.gov.my search 'kecerdasan buatan').

instruments.official_title: Artificial Intelligence Systems Cyber Security Framework (AISCF)
instruments.english_title: Artificial Intelligence Systems Cyber Security Framework (AISCF)
instruments.issuing_authority: National Cyber Security Agency (NACSA), National Security Council, Prime Minister's Department
instruments.current_status: Published by NACSA on its website (framework page and PDF, 60 pages, copyright 2026). The document carries no issue date or version number; the year is taken from its copyright line. It is presented as a framework that complements existing cyber security frameworks and is aligned with the Cyber Security Act 2024 [Act 854]; the text sets no mandatory obligations. A launch on 9 July 2026 is reported only in unofficial sources and is not recorded here.
instruments.scope: All public- and private-sector organisations that develop, deploy, integrate, operate, procure or use AI systems (AI producers, providers, partners and consumers)
instruments.summary: NACSA's framework for securing AI systems across a seven-phase AI secure development lifecycle (inception, design and development, verification and validation, deployment, operation and monitoring, continuous validation and re-evaluation, retirement). It rests on Secure-by-Design, Defence-in-Depth across AI data, AI models and AI infrastructure and applications, and risk-based cyber security governance, and catalogues traditional, AI-specific and emerging risks such as data poisoning, prompt injection, adversarial attacks, model theft and AI supply chain compromise. It assigns shared responsibilities to AI producers, providers, partners and consumers in the public and private sectors, in line with ISO/IEC 42001.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Malaysia's national AI security framework from the national cyber security authority.
metadata_gaps: Exact publication date (only the year 2026 is stated in the document)

instruments.publisher_name: Attorney General's Chambers of Malaysia (Laws of Malaysia portal)
instruments.scope: Data controllers and data processors processing personal data in commercial transactions under the Personal Data Protection Act 2010 [Act 709]
instruments.current_status: In force. Royal Assent 9 October 2024; published in the Gazette 17 October 2024. Brought into operation in three stages by the Minister of Digital under P.U. (B) 522/2024 (dated 19 December 2024, gazetted 24 December 2024): ss. 7, 11, 13, 14 on 1 January 2025; ss. 2, 3, 4, 5, 8, 10, 12 on 1 April 2025; ss. 6 and 9 on 1 June 2025.
instruments.summary: Amends the Personal Data Protection Act 2010 [Act 709]: renames 'data user' as 'data controller', adds 'biometric data' (data from technical processing of physical, physiological or behavioural characteristics) to sensitive personal data, excludes deceased individuals, and makes data processors directly subject to the Security Principle. It requires data controllers and processors to appoint data protection officers, requires data controllers to notify the Commissioner of personal data breaches as soon as practicable (and data subjects where significant harm is likely; fine up to RM250,000 or two years), creates a right to data portability (new s. 43A) and replaces the cross-border transfer whitelist in s. 129 with conditions under which a controller may transfer data abroad. The Act contains no AI-specific provisions but sets the binding rules for personal and biometric data used in training and operating AI systems.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Core amendment of Malaysia's data protection law governing personal and biometric data processed by AI systems; the PDPA framework is the basis for the PDP Commissioner's AI-related guidance.

instruments.publisher_name: Attorney General's Chambers of Malaysia (Laws of Malaysia portal)
instruments.scope: Licensed applications service providers and licensed content applications service providers (and network service providers) under the Communications and Multimedia Act 1998 whose services are used in Malaysia
instruments.current_status: In force since 1 January 2026 (P.U. (B) 449/2025, dated 8 December 2025, gazetted 12 December 2025). Royal Assent 6 May 2025; published in the Gazette 22 May 2025. Subsidiary legislation in force includes the Online Safety (Fees) Regulations 2025 [P.U. (A) 466/2025], the Online Safety (Online Safety Appeal Tribunal) Regulations 2025 [P.U. (A) 478/2025] and, from 1 July 2026, the Online Safety (Online Safety Plan) Regulations 2026 [P.U. (A) 244/2026] and the Online Safety (Compounding of Offences) Regulations 2026 [P.U. (A) 245/2026]; none of these contains AI-specific provisions.
instruments.summary: Regulates harmful online content by imposing duties on licensed applications service providers and content applications service providers: risk-mitigation measures, user guidelines, user safety tools, reporting and user-assistance mechanisms, a mechanism to make priority harmful content (child sexual abuse material and financial fraud) inaccessible, and an Online Safety Plan. Section 18 requires measures for the safe design and operation of services likely to be accessed by children, including measures 'to control personalized recommendation systems suitable for child users'. It establishes an Online Safety Committee and an Online Safety Appeal Tribunal and gives the Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission powers to issue directions and instructions, gather information and impose financial penalties; the Act does not refer expressly to artificial intelligence or AI-generated content.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Binding platform-governance law; regulates harmful content regardless of how it is generated and requires child-safety controls on personalised recommendation (algorithmic) systems.

instruments.official_title: Public Consultation Paper of the Proposed Artificial Intelligence (AI) Governance Bill
instruments.english_title: Public Consultation Paper of the Proposed Artificial Intelligence (AI) Governance Bill
instruments.issuing_authority: National Artificial Intelligence Office (Ministry of Digital)
instruments.publisher_name: Malaysia Productivity Corporation (Unified Public Consultation portal)
instruments.scope: Proposed horizontal AI governance framework covering developers, deployers and other AI actors across all sectors
instruments.current_status: Public consultation held 10 July - 1 August 2026 on the Government's Unified Public Consultation portal (stage: pre-drafting); now closed with a closure report listed. No bill had been gazetted in the Laws of Malaysia portal as of 11 October 2026; the bill itself is held as a lead.
instruments.summary: Consultation by the National AI Office on a proposed AI Governance Bill intended to set a comprehensive, coherent and future-ready AI governance framework for Malaysia. The consultation page states that the proposed Bill would establish central institutional oversight, introduce principle-based national governance requirements, apply a risk-based regulatory framework for proportionate regulation and define the roles and responsibilities of AI actors. Stakeholders were invited to comment on the consultation paper, a questionnaire and a summary document between 10 July and 1 August 2026.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: First proposed horizontal AI law for Malaysia; sets out the intended institutional and risk-based design of a future AI Governance Act.

instruments.official_title: The National Guidelines on AI Governance & Ethics
instruments.english_title: National Guidelines on AI Governance and Ethics (AIGE)
instruments.issuing_authority: Ministry of Science, Technology and Innovation (MOSTI)
instruments.publisher_name: Ministry of Science, Technology and Innovation
instruments.current_status: Launched by the Deputy Prime Minister on 20 September 2024 (MOSTI media release). The PDF on MOSTI's policy page is a revised file dated 18 November 2024. Voluntary; the National AI Action Plan 2026-2030 builds on it, and AI Malaysia's voluntary AI Code of Ethics (AICE) operationalises its seven principles. Publication date source (date audit 2026-10-13): MOSTI media release: 'PUTRAJAYA, 20 September 2024 – YAB Dato' Sri Haji Fadillah ... hari ini telah melancarkan Garis Panduan ... (AIGE)'.
instruments.scope: Malaysia (national); end users, policy makers in government and organisations, and developers, designers, technology providers and suppliers
instruments.summary: MOSTI's voluntary national framework for responsible AI ('AI for Malaysia, AI for All'), built around seven AI principles: fairness; reliability, safety and control; privacy and security; inclusiveness; transparency; accountability; and pursuit of human benefit and happiness. It gives separate guidance for three groups - end users (Part A), policy makers in government, agencies and institutions (Part B, including an independent advisory body) and developers, designers, technology providers and suppliers (Part C, including a code of ethics). It also benchmarks international AI regulation and sets next steps.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Malaysia's core national AI ethics and governance reference; anchors later public-sector and sector guidance.
instruments.evidence_reference: curl (browser user agent, --max-time 60): PDF linked from the MOSTI 'Dasar' page flipbook downloaded and read (138 pages, pdftotext); launch date 20 September 2024 from the MOSTI media release (mosti.gov.my/wp-content/uploads/2024/10/20092024.283925956.pdf).

instruments.official_title: AI Nation 2030: National AI Action Plan 2026-2030
instruments.english_title: AI Nation 2030: National AI Action Plan 2026-2030
instruments.issuing_authority: Ministry of Digital, with AI Malaysia Berhad (National AI Office)
instruments.current_status: Introduced on 28 July 2026 together with the launch of AI Malaysia Berhad by the Prime Minister (AI Malaysia media release of 28 July 2026). The English and Malay PDFs offered on ai.gov.my are versions dated 18 August 2026. Current national AI plan; follows the AI Roadmap 2021-2025.
instruments.summary: Malaysia's national AI plan for 2026-2030, published by the Ministry of Digital and AI Malaysia (National AI Office), succeeding the AI Roadmap 2021-2025. It sets 14 sectoral 'Impact Engine' initiatives (e.g. healthcare, AI cities, public services, public sector, education, agrofood, manufacturing, financial services) and 14 foundational enablers across talent, innovation, data and compute, responsible governance and financing, each with lead ministries and targets. Its governance enablers propose a central AI governance authority with sector regulators, a principles-based risk-based AI regulatory framework as the basis for future AI legislation, a national AI Trust Function (incident monitoring, testing and certification) and a national AI classification.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Current national AI strategy; sets the path toward a risk-based AI regulatory framework, a central AI authority and the Malaysia AI Safety Institute.

It sets six strategies: establishing AI governance, advancing AI R&D, digital infrastructure, AI talent, AI acculturation and a national AI innovation ecosystem, plus national AI use cases. It describes itself as a living document to be revised over time.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Malaysia's first national AI strategy; its governance strategy led to the AIGE guidelines.

instruments.official_title: MMC Guideline on the Ethical Use of Artificial Intelligence (AI) in Medical Practice (Version 1/2025)
instruments.english_title: MMC Guideline on the Ethical Use of Artificial Intelligence (AI) in Medical Practice (Version 1/2025)
instruments.current_status: Endorsed by the MMC Ethics Committee on 29 December 2024 and adopted by the Malaysian Medical Council on 18 February 2025 (note 6.2); due for review within 5 years. Listed on the MMC Laws & Regulations page. The date recorded is the adoption date; no separate publication date is stated.
instruments.scope: Registered medical practitioners in Malaysia using AI tools or technologies in clinical practice
instruments.summary: Ethical guideline of the Malaysian Medical Council for registered medical practitioners using AI in clinical practice, built on WHO principles (autonomy, well-being and safety, transparency and explainability, accountability, privacy). Practitioners remain bound by the MMC Code of Professional Conduct and should only use AI tools that meet 'reasonable confidence' criteria (trustworthiness, appropriateness, transparency, validated conformity to standards, clarity on liability) and should seek training first. It adds consent duties: patients should be told, where appropriate, how AI is used in their care, the basis of AI results, known risks, safeguards and when an AI tool has failed, and practitioners must validate AI outputs under human oversight.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Statutory medical regulator's ethical rules for AI use by doctors.

instruments.issuing_authority: Personal Data Protection Commissioner (Department of Personal Data Protection)
instruments.current_status: Final guideline published on the PDP Commissioner's website (English page dated 30 April 2026 in the page metadata; PDF copyright 2026). Issued under s.48(g) of Act 709 after Public Consultation Paper No. 3/2025 (13 August 2025). Malay version 'Garis Panduan Pembuatan Keputusan Secara Automatik dan Pemprofilan (ADMP)' also listed on the site. The guideline itself states that Act 709 has no specific ADMP provisions and that the guideline supplements the Act. Publication date reduced from 2026-04-30 to 2026 (date audit 2026-10-13): Only date printed in the guideline: '(Department of Personal Data Protection, 2026)' (copyright, PDF p.1). The PDP web page shows no visible date; 30 April 2026 exists only in page metadata (article:published_time), which is not a valid source.
instruments.scope: Data controllers and data processors processing personal data in commercial transactions through automated decision-making or profiling
instruments.summary: Guideline issued by the Personal Data Protection Commissioner under s.48(g) of the PDPA 2010 on automated decision-making (decisions with no or minimal human involvement) and profiling. It requires the Data Protection Officer to be engaged early and a DPIA to be carried out for planned ADMP, and explains notice, consent-withdrawal and sensitive-data rules under Act 709. Part E sets best practices where AI is used for ADMP: assess risks before deployment, tell data subjects in the privacy notice that AI is used, mitigate over-reliance, train staff, never rely on AI as the sole factor in decisions about a data subject, and designate trained human reviewers.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Data protection regulator's guidance on AI-driven automated decision-making and profiling.
metadata_gaps: Issue date not printed in the document; date taken from the official page's publication metadata (30 April 2026)

instruments.official_title: Public Consultation Paper No. 1/2026: Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Personal Data Protection Framework
instruments.english_title: Public Consultation Paper No. 1/2026: Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Personal Data Protection Framework
instruments.issuing_authority: Department of Personal Data Protection (JPDP), Personal Data Protection Commissioner
instruments.current_status: Open for public consultation from 5 October 2026 to 23 October 2026 (feedback to risiko@pdp.gov.my). The full draft framework is in Appendix 1. Malay version 'Kertas Konsultasi Awam Bil. 1/2026: Kerangka Kecerdasan Buatan (AI) dan Perlindungan Data Peribadi' published on the same site. Publication date source (date audit 2026-10-13): Consultation paper cover: 'Start Date: 5 October 2026 ... End Date: 23 October 2026'; PDP page also shows 'October 5, 2026'.
instruments.scope: Data controllers and data processors processing personal data through AI systems (in-house, off-the-shelf, bespoke or embedded via SaaS/API), including general-purpose AI models
instruments.summary: JPDP consultation on a proposed AI and Personal Data Protection Framework under the PDPA 2010, meant to clarify data controllers' and processors' obligations when processing personal data through AI systems, including general-purpose AI models. The draft framework (Parts A-J, Appendix 1) covers legal bases, training-data collection and pre-deployment testing, deployment and decommissioning, due diligence on external AI providers and cross-border transfers, data subject rights, security and bias mitigation, governance and explainability, and lifecycle record-keeping and audits. Comments are invited by 23 October 2026.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Proposed data protection regulator framework specifically for AI systems.

instruments.official_title: Discussion Paper on Artificial Intelligence in the Malaysian Financial Sector
instruments.english_title: Discussion Paper on Artificial Intelligence in the Malaysian Financial Sector
instruments.issuing_authority: Bank Negara Malaysia (Financial Development and Innovation Department)
instruments.current_status: Issued 5 August 2025 for feedback until 17 October 2025; the paper states it is non-binding and may not result in an exposure draft or policy document. Consultation closed; no follow-up exposure draft, policy document or feedback statement on AI was found on the BNM website as of 11 October 2026.
instruments.scope: Financial service providers regulated by BNM (banks, development financial institutions, insurers and takaful operators, e-money issuers)
instruments.summary: BNM's non-binding discussion paper on its posture and proposed regulatory and development approach to AI in the financial sector, drawing on its 2024 AI survey of financial institutions. It takes the view that existing technology-agnostic requirements remain broadly adequate, applies parity, proportionality and neutrality, and expects financial service providers to manage AI risks across the model lifecycle, including data and personal-information controls. It asks for views on a sector-specific AI definition, industry-led guidelines, use of the regulatory sandbox for AI and BNM's development role.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Central bank's proposed approach to AI regulation in the financial sector.

instruments.english_title: Guidelines on Technology Risk Management, including Appendix 3: Guiding Principles relating to the Adoption of Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Machine Learning (ML)
instruments.current_status: Issued 1 August 2023 under s.377 of the Capital Markets and Services Act 2007; revised and effective 19 August 2024 (SC-GL/2-2023 (R1-2024)), superseding the Guidelines on Management of Cyber Risk (2016). The AI/ML guiding principles in Appendix 3 are to be adopted 'where relevant', with entities exercising judgement in proportion to size, scale and complexity; departure from guidance is considered in assessing whether the Guidelines were breached (para 2.05).
instruments.scope: Capital market entities licensed, registered, approved, recognised or authorised by the SC (as defined in para 4.01)
instruments.summary: SC guidelines issued under s.377 CMSA setting technology risk management requirements for capital market entities: board and senior management oversight, technology risk frameworks, technology operations, third-party service providers, cyber security and incident notification. Paragraph 2.04 and Appendix 3 add guiding principles for adopting AI and machine learning: accountability (governance framework, clear roles, ability to suspend AI applications), transparency and explainability of AI-assisted decisions with records for auditability, fairness and non-discrimination with regular review of data and models for bias, and practical accuracy and reliability through validation, testing, data governance and security.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Capital market regulator's AI/ML principles embedded in binding technology risk guidelines.

instruments.official_title: Online Safety Act 2025: Risk Mitigation Code
instruments.english_title: Online Safety Act 2025: Risk Mitigation Code
instruments.current_status: Published 22 May 2026; enforced from 1 June 2026 (cover page). Issued under s.80 of the Online Safety Act 2025 [Act 866] read with s.13; MCMC's FAQ states that failure to comply, as part of a licensed service provider's duties under Part III of ONSA, may lead to enforcement action including a fine or financial penalty of up to RM10 million. Licensed providers may use alternative measures if they satisfy the Commission these better mitigate risk (s.13(2)).
instruments.scope: Licensed applications service providers and licensed content applications service providers using internet access service to enable communications between users or to provide content
instruments.summary: MCMC code under the Online Safety Act 2025 specifying the risk assessment and risk mitigation measures that licensed platform providers must implement to reduce users' exposure to harmful content. Among the measures, providers must test and adapt their algorithmic and recommendation systems to mitigate exposure to harmful content and ensure that generated or manipulated images, audio or video that closely resemble real persons, objects, places or events and could falsely appear authentic are clearly distinguishable through prominent labels or markings, with tools for users and advertisers to disclose such content. New features must be evaluated for risk before deployment.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Binding labelling duty for AI-generated and manipulated (deepfake) content on licensed platforms.

instruments.issuing_authority: Penang State Government (prepared and published by Digital Penang, a state-owned company)
instruments.current_status: Executive summary booklet (82 pp., 'First Printing © 2025', forewords by the Chief Minister of Penang, a State EXCO member and the State Secretary) downloaded from Digital Penang's DEMP page on 11 Oct 2026. The document does not state an exact publication or launch date; the plan covers 2025-2030. The plan states the Penang State Government is the primary driver of DEMP. No separate Penang AI policy or AI guideline for state civil servants was found on official sites.
instruments.summary: Penang's state digital master plan for 2025-2030, succeeding the Digital Transformation Masterplan (DTMP 1.0, 2021-2023) under the Penang2030 vision, organised in four strategic pillars (Digital Government, Digital Economy, Digital Society, Digital Foundation). Under Digital Government action DG-2 it sets a 'Responsible AI in State Government' initiative (DG-2.3, led by the state ICT division BTMKN, target 100% implementation by 2030) alongside a State Digital Governance Framework & Operating Model, and under Digital Foundation it lists AI talent and education actions (PSC AI initiatives, Techdome Penang AI Education Consortium and AI for Schools, State Digital Talent, AI & Innovation Deployment Programme).
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: State digital strategy with a responsible-AI-in-government initiative and AI talent actions.
metadata_gaps: exact publication/launch date not stated in the document (year only)

instruments.issuing_authority: Sarawak Government (Economic Planning Unit Sarawak, Department of the Premier of Sarawak; Sarawak Multimedia Authority)
instruments.publisher_name: Economic Planning Unit Sarawak, Department of the Premier of Sarawak
instruments.current_status: Full blueprint (240 pp.) 'prepared by the Sarawak Government', 'First published in 2023', published by the Economic Planning Unit Sarawak (Department of the Premier) and the Sarawak Multimedia Authority; described in the text as a living document. Downloaded from the Invest Sarawak (state investment agency) 'Roadmaps and Blueprints' page on 11 Oct 2026. Exact launch date not stated in the document. The State AI framework/strategy it calls for is being developed as the Sarawak AI Blueprint (not yet published as of 11 Oct 2026; see leads).
instruments.summary: Sarawak's state digital economy blueprint to 2030, building on the 2018 Sarawak Digital Economy Strategy and anchoring the Post COVID-19 Development Strategy 2030 (PCDS 2030), with five strategic pillars. Its Frontier Technologies Adoption pillar includes strategic action S4 'Catalyse Artificial Intelligence opportunities in public and private sectors', whose AI Adoption Plan initiative (2022-2027, lead agency Sarawak Multimedia Authority) aims to develop an AI action plan, a State AI framework and strategy supporting AI development and ethical deployment, and AI policies, procedures and guidelines for adoption by government and businesses. Further S4 initiatives cover AI-driven forensic timber identification and an AI-focused research and innovation centre.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: State digital strategy with an explicit AI strategic action, including a commitment to a State AI framework and AI guidelines for government.
metadata_gaps: exact publication/launch date not stated in the document (year only)

coverage_audit.no_material_found_note: Technical review notes: Backfill run 2026-10-11 in four parts (M1 federal law via the AGC Laws of Malaysia portal search and the Unified Public Consultation portal; M2 federal government incl. ministry-level search; M3 regulators; M4 top states Selangor, Penang, Sarawak, 30-minute cap per PROTOCOL §6, finished in about 6 minutes). Run in parallel with NGA on separate branches. No interruption. Both earlier records re-checked and fixed (JDN public-sector AI guideline retitled to its Malay title, in force 2025-02-27; NACSA AISCF retitled from the PDF, dated 2026 (copyright year only)); domain-named organisations dropped. ASEAN instruments are attached via the regional files. Merge: the MMC AI ethics guideline came from both M2 and M3 with the same id; its duplicate adoption event dropped. No AI law enacted: the AI Governance Bill consultation paper (UPC, 10 Jul-1 Aug 2026) is behind a portal login (located only); tabling reportedly targeted for 2027 (lead). PDPA 2010 not recorded separately (no AI or automated-decision provisions); CMA and Penal Code amendments 2024-2026, Cyber Security Act 2024 and ONSA regulations checked, no AI provisions. Penang and Sarawak records are digital-economy plans with explicit AI actions; Selangor has no published AI document (AI White Paper in development, lead). Access: parlimen.gov.my unreachable (certificate chain/503), naio.gov.my refused (office now publishes on ai.gov.my; plan PDFs on a content host linked from ai.gov.my), moe.gov.my and moh.gov.my 403, AICE and Boardroom Primer behind a reCAPTCHA form (leads), msonline.gov.my unreachable (mysol.jsm.gov.my used; no Malaysian Standard adoption of ISO/IEC 42001 or other AI standards found), BNM RMiT not read in full for AI provisions. procurement, standards, index-readiness, international: no material found.

leads.note: Proposed horizontal AI law. Public consultation held 10 July - 1 August 2026 (recorded as the consultation instrument). Not tabled in Parliament and not in the Laws of Malaysia portal as of 11 October 2026 (no amendment or principal act with 'artificial intelligence'/'kecerdasan buatan' in its title). Media reports (September-October 2026) say the draft was completed and is going to Cabinet, with tabling targeted for Q1 2027; Parliament's bills page could not be reached to confirm.
